bills.title: Emergency Savings Enhancement Act of 2025
bills.status: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 544.
bills.nexus: S. 3333 likely amends the Internal Revenue Code to expand or create tax-advantaged emergency savings accounts, directly implicating IRS rulemaking authority under Treasury and the Office of Tax Policy. Treasury would bear responsibility for issuing guidance, updating withholding or reporting requirements, and estimating revenue loss, creating both administrative burden and scoring risk.

bills.title: First-Time Home Buyer Empowerment Act
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5227 falls within Treasury's purview because any new first-time homebuyer tax credit or savings incentive would be administered through IRS under Treasury's tax administration authority. The implementation risk centers on designing eligibility rules, preventing fraudulent claims, and estimating revenue cost for the Joint Committee on Taxation score.

bills.title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate that President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service, the resulting settlement from that lawsuit, the purported "Anti-Weaponization Fund", and the purported grant of immunity from tax investigations to the plaintiffs in President Trump's lawsuit, should be rejected, equal protection arguments by others with similar claims should be forestalled, and this settlement should not serve as a precedent and should never be repeated.
bills.status: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary. (text: CR S4436)
bills.nexus: Treasury cares because the resolution directly implicates IRS enforcement authority and settlement practices under the jurisdiction of the Internal Revenue Service, a Treasury bureau. A Senate-expressed rejection of the settlement terms and immunity grants creates political and legal pressure on IRS leadership to revisit or disavow existing agreements, raising litigation exposure and precedent risks for future tax enforcement actions.

bills.title: Senior Accessible Housing Tax Credit Act of 2026
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: Treasury cares because S. 5216 would create a new tax credit administered through the Internal Revenue Service, directly implicating the Office of Tax Policy and IRS's implementation authority under the Internal Revenue Code. The key risks involve revenue scoring, regulatory guidance burdens on IRS, and potential interaction with existing housing credit provisions such as the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit under Section 42.

bills.title: Super Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to the Committee on the Budget, and in addition to the Committee on Rules, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9879 would strengthen budget enforcement rules requiring offsets for legislation that increases mandatory spending or reduces revenues, directly implicating Treasury's Office of Tax Policy and the Office of Fiscal Affairs given their roles in revenue estimation and deficit impact assessments. Treasury bears implementation risk because tightened PAYGO sequestration triggers could constrain tax relief or spending provisions Treasury sponsors and would require close coordination with OMB on scoring and compliance determinations.

bills.title: Data Center Tax Accountability and Disclosure Act of 2026
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5054 falls squarely within Treasury's purview because it would impose new disclosure and accountability requirements tied to tax incentives for data centers, directly implicating the Internal Revenue Service's administration of those provisions under the Tax Code. The implementation risk centers on IRS capacity to design and enforce novel reporting regimes while ensuring the disclosure framework does not create unintended compliance burdens or revenue scoring complications for existing capital investment incentives.

bills.title: To name the Department of Veterans Affairs multispecialty clinic in Marietta, Georgia, as the "Colonel Michael H. Boyce Department of Veterans Affairs Multispecialty Clinic".
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
bills.nexus: This bill is a purely ceremonial VA facility naming measure with no tax, financial, or regulatory provisions touching Treasury's authorities or offices. Treasury has no implementation role, fiscal exposure, or policy equities in this legislation.

bills.title: Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026
bills.status: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 122.
bills.nexus: S. 2354 funds the Departments of Commerce and Justice, which means Treasury's nexus is limited unless floor amendments or conference provisions touch financial crimes enforcement, trade-related revenue functions, or IRS-adjacent appropriations. Treasury should monitor the bill because Commerce's National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) cybersecurity framework funding and Justice's anti-money laundering prosecution resources directly affect Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) operational dependencies and interagency risk posture.
